# My setup

I personally don't have every layout bound. These are my favourites, and when I use them: one example of how layouts, main counts and padding modes fit together. Your screen and keys will differ.

The keys are mine (from [ametrine.sample.yml](../ametrine.sample.yml), which is my config): ⌃⌥ for everyday commands and focus, ⌃⌥⌘ to warp, ⌃⌘ to swap. Numbers in the diagrams are the window order (see [layouts](layouts.md)); "1/3" means 1 window in main and 3 beside it, read left to right.

## On the laptop

A built-in display has room for one or two windows, so I keep it simple.

- **Fullscreen** (⌃⌥1): one window at a time. ⌃⌥H and ⌃⌥L step through the others.
- **Two Pane A** (⌃⌥2): two side by side. The rest wait behind the second one; ⌃⌥J and ⌃⌥K browse them.

{{my-laptop}}

## On the big screen

My big screen is a 55" 4K. [Padding modes](features.md#padding-modes) decide how much of it the windows use, and I pick one for what I'm doing. ⌃⌥0 cycles them, and each Space keeps its own.

- **`full`: entertainment** (a video, a game) or hard work, when I need the whole space.
- **`wide`: multitasking.** The top quarter left free, a 21:9 strip at eye level, so many windows stay in sight at once.
- **`27 screen`: chill.** A centred 27" when I'm just browsing.

{{my-padding}}

### Tall Left: one main thing

The editor or document in main, references stacked beside it. Tall Left has no key of its own: ⌃⌥. and ⌃⌥, cycle to it.

{{my-tall}}

From 1/3 to 2/2: warp a stack window into main (⌃⌥⌘H). A warp into a full main makes room for it.

### 3Column Middle: many windows (⌃⌥3)

Main in the middle, right in front of me; the side columns grow and shrink as I warp windows between them (⌃⌥⌘H / ⌃⌥⌘L).

{{my-3column}}

3/2/3 is 8 windows, about as many as I can keep track of at once: more than that, and I lose the picture.

## Just browsing on the big screen

Fullscreen (⌃⌥1) in `27 screen`: a centred 27" for reading and videos, without the whole 55" in my face.

{{my-browse}}

## Always at hand

- **⌃⌥Z** (`toggle-fullscreen`): one window full size for a moment, in any layout; again to go back.
- **⌃⌥P** (command palette): everything I didn't bind.
- **⌃⌥⇧⌘ F / X / Y** (`flip-twin`, `flip-rows`, `flip-columns`): mirror the layout, or bring the far windows closer. See [flip](layouts.md#flip).
- **Shortcuts…** in the menu bar: all of the above at a glance.
